title: The women, closed
hook: founders, teachers, mothers, queens: the women of the first sangha, gathered up

segments.voice: Yesterday, Mallika, who heard a hard answer and resolved to give. Your line: the generous queen. Did a small gift answer an irritation? Today, we close the women. Day seven hundred sixty-six.

There's a book in the Pali canon made of women's voices: the Therigatha, the verses of the elder nuns. In it, women speak in the first person about leaving home, about grief and children, about bodies and aging, and about the moment their minds were freed. It sits beside the Theragatha, the monks' verses, in the same collection. Several of the women from the last two weeks speak there, in their own lines. For two weeks this path has followed them one at a time. Today we gather them up, and see what they look like standing together.
screen: `A BOOK OF NUNS' VOICES.` → `BESIDE THE MONKS' VERSES.` → `TODAY, ALL OF THEM TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: First, the founders. Mahapajapati, the Buddha's foster mother, who asked for women to go forth, was refused, and asked again, and led the first women into the order. Yasodhara, whom the commentaries remember as the nun Bhadda Kaccana, foremost in great higher knowledge, on a path of her own. Second, the teachers. Khema, whose answer to King Pasenadi matched the Buddha's own. Dhammadinna, whose answers he said he would have given the same way. Patacara, who drew the arrow of grief out of other mothers and was named foremost in the discipline. Third, the mothers and survivors. Uppalavanna, foremost in psychic power, who survived harm and met Mara unafraid. Kisa Gotami, after the mustard seed, in rough robes with a clear mind. Sona, mother of ten, who began late and was named foremost in energy. Fourth, the givers and the queens. Ambapali, who kept the Buddha's meal against the princes and gave her mango grove. Visakha, with her father's riddles and her eight practical requests, a laywoman. Mallika, the queen who heard a hard answer and resolved to give. What runs through all of them? They aren't footnotes in someone else's story. In the texts they get titles of their own, answers of their own to hard questions, and, in the Therigatha, words of their own. One answered a king. One kept the community's rules. One heated the bath water and woke up. Khema in a vision, and Ambapali in her verses, looked straight at aging. The women of the first sangha learned, and they taught. She taught too.
screen: `FOUNDERS: MAHAPAJAPATI, YASODHARA.` · `TEACHERS: KHEMA, DHAMMADINNA, PATACARA.` · `MOTHERS AND SURVIVORS.` · `GIVERS AND QUEENS.` · then, large: `SHE TAUGHT TOO.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: name one woman who taught you. Settle, and breathe. Let one woman come to mind who taught you something that stayed: a mother or grandmother, a teacher, a boss, an aunt, a neighbor, a writer you never met. Maybe someone whose name no one else would know. Say her name silently. What did she teach you? Put it in one sentence. Hold her there a moment, the way the Therigatha holds these women's voices. Then rest with the breath. The bell holds the time.
The women. Founders, teachers, mothers, survivors, givers and queens: the women of the first sangha. Today's word.
Your line: she taught too. Today, pass on one thing the woman you thought of taught you, to someone who could use it, and say where you learned it. Day seven hundred sixty-six.

screen: `DAY 766 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: GOLD COINS ON THE GROUND.`

howItsDone: The Therigatha is read in Theravada communities alongside the monks' verses, and the first nuns and laywomen are remembered by the titles the Buddha's list gives them.

fork.setup: you're Mahapajapati. you've asked the Buddha to let women go forth, and he has refused. what do you do?
fork.reveal: she was refused, asked again, and led the first women into the order.

original.note: Pali theri, an elder nun: the Therigatha is the verses of the theris.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Buddha's early followers were all men.
what it means: founders, teachers, mothers, survivors, givers and queens, each with her own title and story.
what a scholar hears: the list of foremost disciples names women in their own qualities, and the Therigatha preserves verses in their own voices.

notes: Look-back over the women unit (days 753-766). Summaries follow this writer's days 757-765 and the index lines for 753-756 (no scripts for 753-756 were on disk when this was written); check they match whatever those days end up saying, especially Yasodhara and Khema.
Mahapajapati: 'asked, was refused, and asked again' kept vague (the texts give three requests and Ananda's intercession); confirm.
Visakha described as 'a laywoman all her life'; Mallika also a laywoman. Confirm.
Myth item 1 'trapdoor floor 1' about early followers all being men is framed as a common assumption, not a claim about any group.
'It sits beside the Theragatha in the same basket of texts' refers to the Khuddaka Nikaya; confirm.

Editor: checked against days 753-756 now on disk; Yasodhara now named as Bhadda Kaccana, foremost in great higher knowledge, as day 754 says. 'Word for word' softened to 'the same way' (MN 44). 'Some answered kings / some heated the bath water' made singular (one woman each); 'Khema in a mirror... wrote it down' fixed, since Khema saw a vision and wrote nothing. Cut 'all her life' for Visakha and 'basket of texts'. Review question follows day 765's new carry; carry changed so it doesn't repeat day 759's credit-a-teacher carry.

Auditor (y3 audit): myth item 'the Therigatha is a book of the elder nuns' verses' replaced with Sona and the bath water (taught in today's teach); it repeated day 753's Therigatha myth. Summaries checked against days 753-765.
